{{nihongo|'''Ushihiko Shrine'''|宇志比古神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}{{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|Q460812|qid=Q460812}}{{ill|Ōasa-chō Ōtani|Q11442037|qid=Q11442037}}. {{nihongo|'''Ushihiko Shrine'''|宇志比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== History ==
The year of foundation is unknown. During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}–{{ill|1593|Q6772|qid=Q6772}}), the shrine buildings, ancient records, and sacred treasures were destroyed by fire due to an incursion by {{ill|Chōsokabe Motochika|Q1070082|qid=Q1070082}}, but were later rebuilt. During the Edo period it was called Hachiman-gū, and since the Meiji period it has been known as Ushihiko Shrine.

Among extant shrine main halls in Tokushima Prefecture, it is the oldest, and on {{ill|December 4|Q2310|qid=Q2310}}, {{ill|2000|Q1985|qid=Q1985}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 12), the main hall was designated an Important Cultural Property of Japan.
